item.text:
Refactored the design so the tree is no longer tied to `int`. [BinarySearchTree.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/013_binary_search_tree_searching/BinarySearchTree.java) is now a generic `BinarySearchTree<T>` backed by a `Comparator<? super T>`, which makes the implementation reusable for any ordered type instead of only integers. Comparison logic is centralized, null inputs are rejected explicitly with `Objects.requireNonNull`, and the node type was updated to carry generic values cleanly.

I also updated [BinarySearchTreeSearching.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/013_binary_search_tree_searching/BinarySearchTreeSearching.java) to use `BinarySearchTree<Integer>` with the same sample data, so the demo still reflects the original behavior while exercising the more flexible API.

Verification: `javac BinarySearchTree.java BinarySearchTreeSearching.java` succeeded, and `java BinarySearchTreeSearching` still prints `true`.
